summary: @ornikar/eslint-config-babel 24.0.1 ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package's package.json declares a preinstall hook ("preinstall": "node setup.mjs") that runs setup.mjs at npm install time. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line file using hex-name/string-array obfuscation (_0xNNNN identifiers and a shuffled numeric-code array with a rotating decoder) and is not referenced anywhere by the package's advertised ESLint-config surface (index.js only exports lint rules). An ESLint configuration package has no legitimate reason to fetch an alternate language runtime at install time in order to execute an opaque sibling payload; this is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern, and it runs attacker-chosen obfuscated code with the installer's privileges on npm install. The divergence between the package's stated purpose (an @ornikar ESLint config) and the shipped install-time behavior is consistent with a hijacked-maintainer / compromised-publish scenario.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
